title: Refining Labeling Functions with Limited Labeled Data

problem.claim: Studies fixing labeling functions from a small set of labeled examples for programmatic weak supervision.

contributions.claim: Develops repairs that make limited changes on labeled cases while enforcing support for their correct labels and an accuracy requirement for each repaired function.
Represents each labeling function as conditional rules so a repair can target only part of its input space.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their labeling-function repair techniques as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: In experiments, the authors report better labeling-function quality from a limited set of labeled examples.

narrative_sequence.summary: Describes programmatic weak supervision as combining labeling-function outputs on unlabeled data to reduce manual labeling effort.
States that generated-label quality depends on labeling-function accuracy and frames fixing functions from a small labeled set.
Repairs labeling functions with constrained minimal changes and represents them as conditional rules for selective edits.
Reports improved labeling-function quality using small labeled sets.

source_observation.claim: Conditional-rule representations allow output changes on selected inputs while the repair is constrained by labeled examples.

interpretation.claim: A repair procedure can make local changes to rule behavior rather than treating each labeling function as indivisible.

application.claim: For rule-based labeling heuristics, consider whether a representation supports targeted edits grounded in labeled examples.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how broadly the approach applies across labeling-function types or data settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not report dataset names, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
It does not specify the exact repair constraints or labeled-set sizes.
